name: Rewriter API
plain: Rewrites text in a different tone or length on the device.
meaning: Edits what the person typed locally.

access.prompt_ui: Developer origin trial (137 to 148); flag writer-api
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Rewrites text in a different tone or length on the device.

limits.headline: Can rewrite text you typed in a new tone or length, on your device, in testing
limits.user_action: You tap a button like Make shorter or Make friendlier on a site in the trial
can: Change the tone or length of text you typed
Work on your device without a server
Offer a few versions to pick from
cannot: Work for normal visitors yet, since it is an origin trial
Work in Firefox, Safari or on phones
Rewrite text you have not given the page
Run without the browser downloading the model
limits.differs: Only in a Chrome and Edge testing trial today. Not in Firefox, Safari or on phones.

story.what_it_is: A page can rewrite your text in a new tone or length using an AI model on your device.

marketing.name: Rewriter API
marketing.pitch: Lets sites improve text by changing tone or length with Chrome's built in on device AI.

story.for_you: You click a button like Make it shorter or Sound friendlier. The new text appears on screen. The work happens on your device, so your text is not sent out.
story.for_makers: Makers add polish tools without cloud cost or privacy worries. It helps users write faster. It is in testing, so only some users can use it.

use_cases.example: A web email app turns a blunt draft into a polite one with one click.
A post box offers a shorter version that fits a character limit.
A seller tool rewrites a product description in a friendlier voice.
A web editor shortens a long paragraph for a slide.
A customer support tool rewrites a rough reply into a clear message, with no data leaving the device.
A study site rewrites a hard passage in simpler words.
A page rewrites jargon into plain language on request.
